transcripts.text: "Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era" is the latest achievement in the sinicization of Marxism, the crystallization of practical experience and collective wisdom of the Party and the people, an important part of the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the guide to action for the entire Party and the people of the whole country in their efforts to achieve the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. This thought profoundly answers the major questions of what kind of socialism with Chinese characteristics to uphold and develop in the new era and how to uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics. It provides a fundamental guideline for the development of the Party and the country's undertakings in the new era, and has been written into the Party Constitution and the national constitution, becoming the common will of the entire Party and the people of the whole country. We must continue to study, understand, and implement this thought, unswervingly follow the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and strive tirelessly to realize the Chinese Dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

transcripts.text:
**Xi Jinping Thought** (officially *“Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era”*) is the current guiding ideology of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).  It is presented as a continuation and development of the Marxist‑Leninist tradition that the Party has used since its founding, but it is also framed as a distinct set of principles that reflect the leadership’s vision for China’s domestic development and its role in the world.

Below is a concise overview of what the doctrine is, where it comes from, its main content, and why it matters.

---

## 1. Historical and Institutional Context  

| Year | Event | Significance |
|------|-------|--------------|
| **2012** | Xi Jinping becomes General Secretary of the CCP | Begins to articulate a new strategic direction for the Party. |
| **2013** | Xi delivers the speech “*The Governance of China*” (第一卷) | Lays out many of the ideas later codified as “Thought.” |
| **2017** | 19th Party Congress formally enshrines “Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era” in the Party Constitution. | Gives the ideology the same constitutional status as “Mao Zedong Thought” and “Deng Xiaoping Theory.” |
| **2018** | The Constitution of the People’s Republic of China is amended to include Xi Jinping Thought. | Extends the doctrine from Party doctrine to the nation’s supreme legal charter. |
| **2022‑2023** | Publication of the two‑volume *The Governance of China* (第二卷) and the *Xi Jinping Thought* textbook for university curricula. | Institutionalizes the ideology in education and official propaganda. |

---

## 2. How the Party Defines It  

> **“Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is the scientific statement of the Party’s guiding ideology for the new era, the fundamental guideline for the Party’s and the country's work, and the action guide for the Chinese people to achieve the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation.”**  
> — *Pre‑amble to the 19th Party Congress report* (2017)

In practice, the Party treats it as a **“theoretical system”** that integrates political, economic, cultural, social, ecological, and foreign‑policy dimensions.

---

## 3. Core Pillars (the most frequently cited “14‑point” summary)

| # | Pillar (short title) | What it means in plain language |
|---|----------------------|---------------------------------|
| 1 | **The “New Era”** | China has entered a historic period in which its national strength, global influence, and internal development are at a new level. |
| 2 | **The “Chinese Dream”** | The collective aspiration for national rejuvenation, improved living standards, and a strong, prosperous China. |
| 3 | **People‑Centred Development** | Policies must prioritize the welfare of the broad masses, not just economic growth. |
| 4 | **Comprehensive Deepening Reform** | Accelerate reforms across the economy, governance, state‑owned enterprises, the legal system, and the Party itself. |
| 5 | **New Development Concept** (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) | A strategic shift from “quantity‑first” growth to high‑quality, sustainable development. |
| 6 | **Modernisation of the National Governance System** | Strengthen the rule of law, improve administrative efficiency, and make the Party’s leadership more scientific and accountable. |
| 7 | **Socialist Core Values** (prosperity, democracy, civility, harmony, freedom, equality, justice, rule of law) | Ideological education to shape citizens’ moral outlook. |
| 8 | **Ecological Civilization** | Treat the environment as a priority; pursue “green development.” |
| 9 | **National Security** (overall security concept) | Integrate political, economic, cultural, and cyber security under a single strategic framework. |
|10 | **Party’s Absolute Leadership** | The Party must remain the “core” of all political and social life; “the Party leads everything.” |
|11 | **The “Four Comprehensives”** (comprehensively build a moderately prosperous society; comprehensively deepen reform; comprehensively govern the nation according to law; comprehensively strictly govern the Party) | A four‑point action plan that underpins all policy. |
|12 | **“One Belt, One Road” (Belt‑and‑Road Initiative)** | Use infrastructure, trade, and investment to build a global network of connectivity and Chinese influence. |
|13 | **Community of Shared Future for Mankind** | Promote a multilateral, win‑win approach to global governance; oppose “hegemonic” policies. |
|14 | **Strict Party Discipline & Anti‑Corruption** | Continue the sweeping anti‑corruption campaign; enforce loyalty, integrity, and ideological purity within the Party. |

*Note:* Different official documents list 12, 13, or 14 points; the above captures the most widely cited set.

---

## 4. How It Differs From Earlier Ideologies  

| Earlier Doctrine | Main Focus | Xi Jinping Thought adds/changes |
|------------------|-----------|--------------------------------|
| **Mao Zedong Thought** (1940s‑1970s) | Class struggle, mass mobilization, “continuous revolution.” | Moves away from class struggle as a primary driver; emphasizes stability, modernization, and “peaceful development.” |
| **Deng Xiaoping Theory** (1978‑1990s) | “Socialism with Chinese characteristics,” “reform and opening up,” “Four Modernizations.” | Retains reform but adds a stronger political‑ideological component (Party supremacy) and a more explicit global vision. |
| **Three Represents** (Jiang Zemin, 1997) | Party represents advanced productive forces, culture, and the majority’s interests. | Broadens the “people‑centred” claim, but Xi’s Thought stresses “national rejuvenation” and a more assertive foreign policy. |
| **Scientific Outlook on Development** (Hu Jintao, early 2000s) | Harmonious, sustainable development, “building a moderately prosperous society.” | Introduces the “new development concept,” a more explicit ecological agenda, and the “new era” narrative. |

In short, Xi Jinping Thought **re‑centers the Party’s absolute authority**, **integrates domestic reforms with an assertive foreign policy**, and **frames China’s rise as a historic mission** rather than a mere economic catch‑up.

---

## 5. Institutional Manifestations  

1. **Party Constitution** – Article 9 explicitly states that “the Party must uphold Xi Jinping Thought… as the guiding ideology.”  
2. **State Constitution** – The preamble of the 2018 amendment mentions “the guiding principle of Xi Jinping Thought.”  
3. **Education** – Textbooks on “Xi Jinping Thought” are mandatory in primary, secondary, and university curricula; the Party runs “Study Xi Jinping Thought” campaigns for cadres.  
4. **Media & Propaganda** – State media (Xinhua, CCTV, People's Daily) regularly publish articles and commentaries interpreting current events through the lens of Xi Jinping Thought.  
5. **Policy Documents** – Five‑year plans, the “14th Five‑Year Plan” (2021‑2025), and the “14th Party Congress” report all cite the Thought as the strategic foundation.

---

## 6. Why It Matters  

| Dimension | Impact |
|-----------|--------|
| **Domestic Governance** | Provides a unifying ideological banner for the CCP’s tightening control over the civil society, the internet, and the military. |
| **Economic Policy** | Guides the shift toward high‑tech, green, and self‑reliant growth; underpins policies like “Made in China 2025,” “dual circulation,” and the crackdown on “disordered capital.” |
| **Foreign Policy** | Justifies a more proactive, sometimes confrontational stance (e.g., in the South China Sea, Taiwan, and trade disputes) while promoting the Belt‑and‑Road Initiative and the “global community of shared future.” |
| **International Perception** | Signals to other states that China’s rise is framed as a civilizational mission, not merely a commercial one; influences how other governments formulate their own China strategies. |
| **Party Legitimacy** | By linking the Party’s success to the “Chinese Dream,” the ideology seeks to cement popular support and pre‑empt dissent. |

---

## 7. Common Criticisms & Scholarly Views  

| Critique | Explanation |
|----------|-------------|
| **Personality Cult** | Critics argue that the elevation of Xi’s name to the level of “Thought” creates a quasi‑cult of personality reminiscent of Mao’s era. |
| **Ideological Vagueness** | Some scholars note that the language is deliberately broad, allowing the Party to apply it to a wide range of policies without clear constraints. |
| **Centralization of Power** | The doctrine is used to justify the removal of term limits (2018) and the concentration of decision‑making in Xi’s hands. |
| **Human‑Rights Concerns** | The emphasis on “national security” and “strict Party discipline” has been linked to increased surveillance, repression in Xinjiang, Hong Kong, and tighter control over NGOs. |
| **Economic Risks** | The push for “self‑reliance” and “dual circulation” may lead to protectionist measures that could hamper foreign investment and global supply‑chain integration. |

Nevertheless, many analysts also point out that the Thought **provides a coherent narrative** that helps the CCP maintain internal cohesion during a period of rapid change and external pressure.

---

## 8. Quick Take‑away  

- **What it is:** The official, Party‑endorsed ideological framework that defines China’s political, economic, and diplomatic direction under Xi Jinping.  
- **Core message:** “The Party leads everything; China is in a new era of rejuvenation; development must be people‑centred, high‑quality, and globally responsible.”  
- **Why it matters:** It is now the *constitutional* basis for policy‑making, education, and Party discipline, shaping everything from local governance to China’s interaction with the rest of the world.

---

### Further Reading (for deeper dives)

1. **Party Documents** – *Report of the 19th National Congress of the CCP* (2017); *Constitution of the CCP* (2022 amendment).  
2. **Xi Jinping, *The Governance of China* (Volumes I‑III)** – Collections of speeches and essays that articulate the Thought.  
3. **Scholarly Analyses** –  
   - Cheng, Li. *“Xi Jinping’s Thought: Ideology, Power, and Governance.”* *Journal of Contemporary China* (2021).  
   - Shambaugh, David. *“China’s New Era: The Rise of Xi Jinping.”* *Foreign Affairs* (2020).  
4. **Think‑Tank Reports** – Brookings Institution, “Understanding Xi Jinping Thought” (2022); Carnegie Endowment, “The Political Economy of Xi’s Ideology” (2023).  

Feel free to ask if you’d like a deeper explanation of any specific pillar, its implementation in a particular sector, or how it compares to other world leaders’ governing philosophies.

transcripts.text:
**“习近平思想”（全称：习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想）**是中国共产党在 21 世纪提出的指导思想，是在马克思主义、列宁主义、毛泽东思想、邓小平理论、“三个代表”重要思想、科学发展观的基础上形成的、适应新时代中国发展要求的最新理论成果。它自 2012 年习近平担任中共中央总书记以来逐步形成、系统化，并于 2017 年第十九次全国代表大会正式写入《中国共产党章程》，随后在 2018 年的《中华人民共和国宪法修正案》中写入宪法序言，成为国家层面的根本指导思想。

下面从 **形成背景、核心要义、主要内容、实践意义** 四个方面系统阐述“习近平思想”。

---

## 一、形成背景

| 时间节点 | 关键事件 | 思想萌芽 |
|----------|----------|----------|
| 2012 年 11 月 | 习近平当选中共中央总书记 | 开始提出“全面深化改革”“全面依法治国”等新概念 |
| 2013 年 3 月 | 习近平在全国两会作政府工作报告 | 提出“新发展理念”“供给侧结构性改革” |
| 2014 年 10 月 | 在中央政法工作会议上提出“全面依法治国” | 强调法治与党的领导的统一 |
| 2015 年 9 月 | 在纪念改革开放 35 周年大会上发表讲话 | 明确“坚持和发展中国特色社会主义”进入新时代 |
| 2017 年 10 月 | 党的十九大正式将“习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想”写入党章 | 思想体系基本定型 |
| 2020 年 10 月 | 党的十九届五中全会进一步深化对该思想的阐释 | 强调“十四五”规划与实现中华民族伟大复兴的关系 |

**时代特征**：进入 21 世纪后，中国已由“高速增长”阶段转向“高质量发展”阶段，国内外环境出现深刻变化（如全球化逆流、科技革命、地缘政治竞争等），这要求党必须提出适应新形势的系统理论来指导实践。

---

## 二、核心要义（“八个明确”和“十四个坚持”）

### 1. “八个明确”

1. **明确坚持和发展中国特色社会主义，总任务是实现中华民族伟大复兴**。  
2. **明确新时代的历史方位**：我国社会主要矛盾已转化为“人民日益增长的美好生活需要和不平衡不充分的发展之间的矛盾”。  
3. **明确全面深化改革的总目标**：完善和发展中国特色社会主义制度，推进国家治理体系和治理能力现代化。  
4. **明确新发展理念**：创新、协调、绿色、开放、共享。  
5. **明确人民主体地位**：坚持以人民为中心的发展思想，保障和改善民生。  
6. **明确全面依法治国**：建设中国特色社会主义法治体系，建设社会主义法治国家。  
7. **明确坚持党对一切工作的领导**：党的领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征。  
8. **明确坚持总体国家安全观**：统筹发展和安全，维护国家主权、安全、发展利益。

### 2. “十四个坚持”

1. **坚持党对一切工作的领导**  
2. **坚持以人民为中心**  
3. **坚持全面深化改革**  
4. **坚持新发展理念**  
5. **坚持人民当家作主**（社会主义民主政治）  
6. **坚持全面依法治国**  
7. **坚持社会主义核心价值体系**  
8. **坚持在发展中保障和改善民生**  
9. **坚持人与自然和谐共生**（生态文明）  
10. **坚持总体国家安全观**  
11. **坚持党对军队的绝对领导**  
12. **坚持“一国两制”和推进祖国统一**  
13. **坚持构建人类命运共同体**（大国外交）  
14. **坚持全面从严治党**  

这“八个明确”与“十四个坚持”相互支撑，构成了习近平思想的理论框架。

---

## 三、主要内容与重点领域

| 领域 | 关键概念 | 具体体现 |
|------|----------|----------|
| **经济** | **新发展理念**、**供给侧结构性改革**、**高质量发展** | 推动创新驱动、产业升级、数字经济、绿色低碳转型 |
| **政治** | **坚持党的全面领导**、**人民当家作主**、**全面依法治国** | 党内政治生活规范化、完善人民代表大会制度、深化司法体制改革 |
| **文化** | **社会主义核心价值观**、**中华优秀传统文化创造性转化** | 加强思想舆论引导、提升国家文化软实力 |
| **社会** | **以人民为中心**、**共同富裕**、**精准扶贫** | 完善社会保障、教育公平、健康中国、乡村振兴 |
| **生态** | **绿色发展**、**人与自然和谐共生** | 推进碳达峰、碳中和、生态保护红线、污染防治 |
| **国防与军队** | **党对军队的绝对领导**、**强军目标** | 深化国防和军队改革、提升信息化作战能力 |
| **外交** | **构建人类命运共同体**、**新型国际关系** | “一带一路”、全球治理、维护多边主义、推动大国外交 |
| **党的建设** | **全面从严治党**、**党风廉政建设** | 反腐败斗争、制度化监督、干部人事制度改革 |

### 1. **创新驱动与科技自立**
- 强调把科技创新摆在国家发展全局的核心位置，提出“实现关键核心技术自主可控”。  
- 推动“大基金”“国家实验室”“双创”政策，培育新一代信息技术、人工智能、生物技术等战略性新兴产业。

### 2. **共同富裕**
- 不是平均主义，而是通过收入分配制度改革、公共服务均等化、区域协调发展等手段，让发展成果更多更公平惠及全体人民。  
- 重点在于缩小城乡、区域、行业之间的收入差距，防止极端贫富分化。

### 3. **总体国家安全观**
- 把政治安全、领土安全、军事安全、经济安全、文化安全、社会安全、科技安全、网络安全、生态安全、资源安全、核安全等 11 大安全维度纳入统一布局。  
- 强调“安全是发展的前提，发展是安全的保障”。

### 4. **人类命运共同体**
- 主张在全球化背景下，各国相互依存、共同发展，反对单边主义和保护主义。  
- 通过“一带一路”倡议、构建新型国际关系、推动全球治理体系改革等方式，提升中国在国际事务中的话语权。

---

## 四、实践意义与影响

### 1. **理论创新的历史定位**
- 将马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际和时代特征相结合，形成了适用于“新时代”的系统理论。  
- 为党在新的历史条件下坚持和发展中国特色社会主义提供了行动指南。

### 2. **政策制定的根本依据**
- 党和国家的重大决策（如《十四五规划》《2035年远景目标纲要》）均以习近平思想为指导原则。  
- 各级政府在制定经济、社会、生态、文化等政策时，都要对照“八个明确”“十四个坚持”进行评估。

### 3. **治理体系现代化**
- 强调“治理体系和治理能力现代化”，推动法治、信息化、数字治理、社会治理创新。  
- 通过“数字政府”“智慧城市”等手段提升公共服务效率。

### 4. **国际形象与软实力提升**
- “构建人类命运共同体”与“一带一路”成为中国对外宣传的核心概念，提升了中国在发展中国家和全球治理中的影响力。  
- 通过文化交流、媒体合作、国际合作项目，向世界展示中国的治理经验。

### 5. **党内政治生活的规范化**
- “全面从严治党”使党内监督、干部选拔、廉政建设制度化、常态化。  
- 通过巡视、审计、纪检监察等机制，强化党内政治生态。

---

## 五、常见的争议与批评（客观呈现）

| 争议点 | 主要观点 | 说明 |
|--------|----------|------|
| **意识形态的集中化** | 有学者担心思想的高度集中可能抑制学术多元与公共讨论 | 党强调统一思想是维护政治稳定的必要手段，但也需要在制度层面保障言论与学术自由的空间 |
| **“共同富裕”与市场活力** | 部分企业界人士担心过度的再分配会削弱创新激励 | 实际政策更侧重于完善税制、提升公共服务，而非直接限制企业利润 |
| **对外政策的“大国外交”** | 有观察者认为中国在推动“人类命运共同体”时，兼具软硬实力的双重压力 | 中国在多边机构中积极参与，同时在地区安全、海洋权益等方面保持强硬立场 |
| **法治与党的领导的关系** | 法律学者关注“党领导法治”是否会导致司法独立受限 | 党强调法治是党的领导的保障，实际操作中通过司法体制改革、审判公开等方式提升透明度 |

# Xi Jinping Thought

**"Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era"** is the official political ideology and theoretical framework associated with Xi Jinping, the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and President of China.

## Key Facts

- **Adopted**: Enshrined into the CCP's constitution in October 2017, and later added to China's state constitution in 2018
- **Status**: Placed alongside Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought, and Deng Xiaoping Theory as part of the party's official ideological canon
- **Significance**: Xi is only the third leader (after Mao and Deng) to have his name directly attached to an ideology while still in power, signaling his consolidated political authority

## Core Elements

The ideology covers a broad range of policy areas, often summarized as containing **14 principles**, including:

1. Ensuring CCP leadership over all forms of work in China
2. Pursuing "people-centered" development
3. Continuing "reform and opening up"
4. Following a "new development philosophy" (innovation, coordination, green development, opening up, and sharing)
5. Ensuring the rule of law
6. Promoting "socialist core values"
7. Improving living standards
8. Prioritizing ecological conservation
9. Strengthening national security
10. Ensuring absolute Party control over the military
11. Advancing "one country, two systems" (regarding Hong Kong/Macau) and national reunification (regarding Taiwan)
12. Building a global community with a "shared future for mankind" (related to Belt and Road Initiative diplomacy)
13. Building the CCP itself through strict governance
14. Pursuing the "Chinese Dream" of national rejuvenation

## Political Significance

- Reinforces centralized Party control, particularly under Xi's leadership
- Used to justify increased state control over the economy, society, and technology
- Integrated into education curricula, from primary schools to universities
- Serves as a tool for maintaining ideological discipline within the Party

Critics view it as a vehicle for consolidating personal power, while supporters frame it as a necessary evolution of socialist theory suited to China's contemporary challenges.

# 习近平思想

严格来说,目前正式的官方术语是**"习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想"**,通常简称为"习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想"或口语中简称"习近平思想"。

## 基本情况

**确立过程：**
- 2017年中共十九大写入党章
- 2018年写入中国宪法
- 2021年被确立为党的"两个确立"之一(确立习近平同志党中央的核心、全党的核心地位，确立习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的指导地位)

## 主要内容

这一思想体系通常被概括为"十个明确"和"十四个坚持"，涵盖以下核心方面：

1. **坚持和发展中国特色社会主义** - 总目标、总任务
2. **全面深化改革** - 完善和发展中国特色社会主义制度
3. **依法治国** - 全面推进法治建设
4. **党的领导** - 强调党对一切工作的领导
5. **经济发展** - 新发展理念、供给侧改革等
6. **生态文明** - "绿水青山就是金山银山"
7. **强军强国** - 国防和军队现代化
8. **外交理念** - "人类命运共同体"、"一带一路"
9. **反腐倡廉** - 全面从严治党
10. **民族复兴** - "中国梦"的实现路径

## 性质定位

官方将其定位为：
- 马克思主义中国化的最新成果
- 中国特色社会主义理论体系的最新发展
- 全党全国人民为实现中华民族伟大复兴而奋斗的行动指南

## 需要说明的是

对这一思想体系的评价存在不同视角：
- **官方视角**：视为对马克思主义、毛泽东思想、邓小平理论等的继承和发展
- **学术/国际视角**：有学者从政治学角度分析其与个人权力集中、意识形态建设等方面的关系
- **历史比较视角**：有观察者将其与此前领导人思想的地位进行比较讨论

如果你需要了解某个具体方面(如某项具体政策、理论渊源、或某个国际观察角度的分析)，可以告诉我，我可以提供更详细的信息。

**“习近平思想”**，全称为**“习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想”**，是中国共产党现行的核心指导思想，也是中华人民共和国宪法和中国共产党章程所确立的国家意识形态和行动指南。

该思想以中共中央总书记习近平的名字命名，标志着其在党内拥有与毛泽东、邓小平并列的理论权威地位。

以下从**提出背景、核心内涵、主要领域和政治意义**四个方面为您详细梳理：

---

### 一、 提出的背景与确立过程

* **提出：** 2017年10月，在中共十九大上，该思想被正式提出并写入《中国共产党章程》。
* **入宪：** 2018年3月，在第十三届全国人民代表大会第一次会议上，该思想被写入《中华人民共和国宪法》序言。
* **时代背景（“新时代”）：** 官方认为，中国特色社会主义进入了“新时代”。我国社会的主要矛盾已经转化为**“人民日益增长的美好生活需要和不平衡不充分的发展之间的矛盾”**（取代了过去的“人民日益增长的物质文化需要同落后的社会生产之间的矛盾”）。

---

### 二、 核心理论体系

官方通常用**“十个明确”**、**“十四个坚持”**和**“十三个方面成就”**来概括其理论架构：

1. **“十个明确”（理论层面的核心内容）：**
   * **总任务：** 实现社会主义现代化和中华民族伟大复兴（分两步走，到本世纪中叶建成富强民主文明和谐美丽的社会主义现代化强国）。
   * **根本领导：** 明确中国共产党领导是中国特色社会主义最本质的特征，是“最大的优势”，强调**“党政军民学，东西南北中，党是领导一切的”**。
   * **发展布局：** 统筹推进“五位一体”（经济、政治、文化、社会、生态文明建设），协调推进“四个全面”战略布局。
   * **新发展理念：** 创新、协调、绿色、开放、共享。
   * **国防与军队：** 建设一支听党指挥、能打胜仗、作风优良的人民军队。
   * **大国外交：** 推动构建“人类命运共同体”，推进“一带一路”建设。

2. **“十四个坚持”（行动层面的基本方略）：**
   * 包括坚持党对一切工作的领导、坚持以人民为中心、坚持全面深化改革、坚持全面依法治国、坚持总体国家安全观、“一国两制”和推进祖国统一等。

---

### 三、 细分领域思想

随着时间推移，该思想在各个具体领域进行了系统化阐述，主要包括：

* **习近平经济思想：** 强调高质量发展、供给侧结构性改革、“双循环”新发展格局（国内大循环为主体、国内国际双循环相互促进）、统筹发展与安全。
* **习近平法治思想：** 强调“全面依法治国”，将法治与党的领导相统一。
* **习近平生态文明思想：** 提出**“绿水青山就是金山银山”**，强调绿色低碳发展和碳达峰、碳中和目标。
* **习近平强军思想：** 强调政治建军、改革强军、科技强军、依法治军，确保军队绝对听党指挥。
* **习近平外交思想：** 倡导“中国特色大国外交”，推动全球治理体系变革，核心概念是构建“人类命运共同体”。
* **习近平文化思想（2023年正式提出）：** 强调文化自信、意识形态安全，以及将马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合（即“第二个结合”）。

---

### 四、 政治意义与历史地位

在当代中国政治话语体系中，习近平思想具有极高的地位：

1. **马克思主义中国化的新飞跃：** 中共将其定性为“当代中国马克思主义、二十一世纪马克思主义”，是继毛泽东思想、邓小平理论之后的又一次重大理论飞跃。
2. **巩固政治核心地位：** 该思想的确立与**“两个确立”**（确立习近平同志党中央的核心、全党的核心地位，确立习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的指导地位）和**“两个维护”**紧密相连，为现行政治体制提供了理论合法性和凝聚力。
3. **中国式现代化：** 它提出了区别于西方现代化路径的“中国式现代化”概念，强调不走西方资本主义的老路，而是通过国家主导、共同富裕和物质文明与精神文明相协调的方式实现现代化。

总结来说，“习近平思想”是指导当代中国内政、外交、经济、军事、法律和文化等全方位国家治理的**总体政治纲领和意识形态体系**。

**"Xi Jinping Thought"**—officially titled **"Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era"**—is the official political philosophy and guiding ideology of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and the People’s Republic of China (PRC), named after its current leader, General Secretary Xi Jinping.

First unveiled at the 19th CCP National Congress in October 2017, it was written into both the CCP Constitution (2017) and the State Constitution (2018). This elevated Xi Jinping to the same ideological status as Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, cementing his position as China’s most powerful leader in decades.

Here is a breakdown of its core concepts, pillars, and significance:

---

### 1. The Core Premise: The "New Era"
Xi’s ideology posits that China has entered a **"New Era"** of historical development. According to the CCP's official historical narrative:
1. **Under Mao Zedong:** China "stood up" (achieved sovereignty and ended foreign subjugation).
2. **Under Deng Xiaoping:** China "grew rich" (economic reform and opening up).
3. **Under Xi Jinping:** China is "becoming strong" (achieving global power, technological leadership, and domestic stability).

Xi also redefined the "principal contradiction" facing Chinese society. Previously, it was seen as the gap between "the backward productive forces and the people’s material needs" (poverty). Xi redefined it as the gap between **"unbalanced and inadequate development and the people’s ever-growing needs for a better life"**—meaning focus must shift from pure GDP growth to quality of life, equality, and environmental protection.

---

### 2. Core Pillars of Xi Jinping Thought
While the official doctrine includes "14 Fundamental Principles," it can be summarized into several key themes:

#### A. Absolute Party Leadership
* **The Party Leads Everything:** Xi famously revived the Mao-era slogan: *"Party, government, military, society, and education; east, west, south, north, and center, the Party leads everything."* 
* The CCP is positioned as the only institution capable of holding China together and driving its modern rise. Xi has cracked down on dissent, centralized control, and eliminated alternative power centers (including curbing the independence of private tech giants).

#### B. The "Chinese Dream" and National Rejuvenation
* The goal is the **"Great Rejuvenation of the Chinese Nation"** by 2049 (the centenary of the PRC).
* This includes achieving full modernization, erasing historical humiliations, and ensuring territorial integrity—most notably bringing **Taiwan** under Beijing's control.

#### C. Economic Strategy and "Common Prosperity"
* **High-Quality Growth:** Moving away from debt-fueled, export-driven growth toward innovation, advanced technology (semiconductors, AI, green tech), and domestic consumer demand (known as the "Dual Circulation" strategy).
* **Common Prosperity (共同富裕):** A push to reduce the extreme wealth gap through taxation, social welfare, regulation of private wealth, and pressure on mega-corporations to invest in social goods.
* **State Guidance:** A belief that the state should guide the market, maintaining strong control over strategic sectors through State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs).

#### D. Total National Security
* National security is viewed holistically, covering not just the military, but the economy, ideology, internet/data, culture, and public health.
* It emphasizes rapid military modernization to make the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) a "world-class military" capable of fighting and winning wars by mid-century.

#### E. Ecological Civilization (Green Development)
* Environmental protection is integrated into state ideology. Xi’s famous slogan is: *"Clear waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets"* (literally "as good as gold and silver").
* This underpins China’s massive domestic investment in renewable energy and its commitment to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060.

#### F. Assertive Foreign Policy
* Moving away from Deng Xiaoping’s foreign policy principle of "hide your strength, bide your time" (*tao guang yang hui*), Xi’s ideology advocates a confident, proactive global role.
* Key initiatives include the **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**, the **Global Security Initiative (GSI)**, and promoting a **"Community with a Shared Future for Mankind"**—an alternative to the Western-led liberal international order.

---

### 3. How It Is Implemented in Practice
* **Education and Society:** Xi Jinping Thought has been integrated into school and university curricula across China, from primary schools to graduate programs.
* **The "Xuexi Qiangguo" App:** Millions of CCP members, civil servants, and state workers use a state-developed smartphone app ("Study to Make China Strong") to read articles, take quizzes on Xi’s ideology, and earn points.
* **Corporate Governance:** Private and foreign companies operating in China have been pressured to establish internal CCP branches to ensure alignment with party objectives.

---

### 4. Significance and Criticisms

* **Ideological Supremacy:** In CCP political culture, having an ideology named after you while still in office (like Mao, but unlike Deng, whose "Theory" was canonized posthumously) makes any criticism of the leader’s policies an attack on the Party itself.
* **Shift from Collective Leadership:** Critics argue that Xi Jinping Thought has dismantled the collective leadership model established by Deng Xiaoping to prevent another Mao-like figure, instead institutionalizing a personality cult and life-tenure leadership.
* **Economic Concerns:** Western analysts and private business leaders often argue that the doctrine’s emphasis on state control and ideology over market mechanisms has stifled private-sector innovation and contributed to China’s recent economic slowdown.
* **Geopolitical Tensions:** The assertive nationalism inherent in Xi Jinping Thought has contributed to heightened friction with the United States, neighboring countries in the South China Sea, and democratic nations concerned about human rights and the future of Taiwan.
